$comment: Facts from a detection vector assay post-excision. A dCas9-VPR reporter vector targeting the same HSV-2 signatures was delivered to sacral DRG neurons 14 days after excision therapy. GFP fluorescence was quantified per cell.

facts.note: 12/847 neurons showed residual HSV signature (1.4%). This is a measured upper bound on residual viral DNA. Whether 98.6% clearance constitutes 'elimination' is a threshold question the system does not answer — it reports the measurement.

subject.sensitivity: detects single-copy HSV genome per cell
subject.specificity: no cross-reactivity with host genome confirmed by negative control

data.method: dCas9-VPR-GFP reporter + single-cell sequencing of dark cells
data.note: Measured in 847 sacral DRG neurons from 6 human organoid samples. 89% deletion + 3.5% degradation = 92.5% successful excision per copy. 1.4% uncut (residual). Rejoined and inverted outcomes are named and counted — the system does not silently count them as success.
